injuries.longComment: Paopao has already missed the last two games with a right leg injury and can be considered week-to-week moving forward. In the meantime, Isobel Borlase will likely see a bump in minutes off the bench.
injuries.shortComment: Paopao (leg) will be re-evaluated in "the coming weeks," WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.

injuries.longComment: Nivar will be inactive for the third straight game in an effort to preserve her eligibility on a developmental contract. The guard's next opportunity to play will come after the All-Star break, July 29 against Dallas.
injuries.shortComment: Nivar (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Chicago.

injuries.longComment: Carrington, who went through a full practice session Tuesday, is aiming to make her season debut Thursday following a lengthy recovery from offseason foot surgery. She'd figure to have a minutes restriction if cleared to suit up, but Carrington could eventually push Gabriela Jaquez and Jacy Sheldon for a significant role off the bench.
injuries.shortComment: Carrington (foot) is officially listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Sun.

injuries.longComment: Stevens is attending to a personal matter and is unavailable for the first time since May 20. Her next chance to rejoin the team comes during Saturday's showdown against the defending-champion Aces. Gabriela Jaquez appears to be the most likely candidate to replace Stevens in the starting lineup Thursday.
injuries.shortComment: Stevens is out for Thursday's game against the Sun for personal reasons.

injuries.longComment: The veteran guard has been on the shelf since early July with a right knee injury and doesn't sound to be on the verge of returning to game action. Sydney Taylor and Courtney Vandersloot should remain the primary fantasy beneficiaries of Diggins' continued absence in the backcourt.
injuries.shortComment: Head coach Tyler Marsh said Monday that Diggins (knee) is considered week-to-week, per Chicago State of Mind Sports.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: Westbeld is able to make only 12 regular-season appearances under a developmental deal and will be ruled out more often than not in 2026. Her next chance to play is July 30 against the Sun.
injuries.shortComment: Westbeld (coach's decision) is out for Wednesday's game against the Liberty,

injuries.longComment: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.
injuries.shortComment: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.

injuries.longComment: Edwards was initially tabbed as probable for Tuesday's contest against the Mystics, so it's possible she's since suffered a setback in her recovery from a right knee injury. Fresh off delivering a career-high 21 points her last time out, Aneesah Morrow should continue to provide enhancing streaming appeal in Edwards' absence Thursday.
injuries.shortComment: Edwards (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Sky.

injuries.longComment: The veteran center is sidelined for a third straight contest due to a left knee injury. Kennedy Burke and Aneesah Morrow should help pick up the slack in the frontcourt Thursday.
injuries.shortComment: Griner (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Sky.

injuries.longComment: Van Lith will be held out of Tuesday's contest in an effort to manage her eligibility while signed to a developmental pact. Her next opportunity to play will come in Chicago on Thursday.
injuries.shortComment: Van Lith (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Mystics.

injuries.longComment: Jackson will be ruled out more often than not due to her limited availability under a developmental contract. Her next chance to take the court comes Thursday against the Sky.
injuries.shortComment: Jackson (coach's decision) is out for Tuesday's game against the Mystics.

injuries.longComment: Williams will miss her second game of the 2026 campaign Wednesday. However, Golden State won't play again until Sunday against Toronto, meaning she could be back for that contest. In the meantime, Kaila Charles, who started in Williams' place in the 79-64 win over Connecticut, could re-enter the starting lineup. If anything, Charles is expected to see more playing time. That should also apply to Janelle Salaun and Tiffany Hayes.
injuries.shortComment: Williams (reconditioning) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Phoenix.

injuries.longComment: Rupert signed a multi-year contract with Golden State during the offseason and missed the start of training camp due to an overseas commitment. Her status for the 2026 regular season now appears to be in jeopardy due to her pregnancy. The 24-year-old made 21 regular-season appearances (11 starts) for the Valkyries last year and averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.1 minutes per game. If Rupert is sidelined in 2026, Janelle Salaun, Kiah Stokes and Laeticia Amihere are candidates to see increased work.
injuries.shortComment: Rupert is pregnant, and the Valkyries have filed for a replacement contract ahead of the 2026 season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports Thursday.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: Hall was listed as probable before tipoff, and it's unclear if she was available to play. The developmental player's next chance to suit up will come in Portland on Friday.
injuries.shortComment: Hall (ankle) didn't play in Tuesday's 105-95 win over the Storm.

injuries.longComment: Dantas will miss a second consecutive contest due to a left knee injury. She's currently away from the team and can be considered highly questionable for Friday's game in Portland until the Fever offer an update on her status.
injuries.shortComment: Dantas (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Storm.

injuries.longComment: Bell is likely to miss her fifth consecutive game Thursday, but this is the first time she's received the doubtful tag since going down with the leg injury, indicating progress. Justine Pissott and Dana Evans will continue to pick up the slack in Bell's absence.
injuries.shortComment: Bell (leg) is doubtful for Thursday's game against the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: Parker-Tyus will miss her second consecutive game Thursday, meaning her next opportunity to suit up will come Saturday in Chicago. With NaLyssa Smith (undisclosed) and Kierstan Bell (leg) also on the injury report, Brianna Turner, who made her first start of the 2026 campaign in Tuesday's 98-83 win over Portland and logged a season-high 32 minutes, could remain in line for more action.
injuries.shortComment: Parker-Tyus (concussion) is listed as out for Thursday's game against New York.

injuries.longComment: Head coach Becky Hammon said Wednesday afternoon that she was expecting Smith to play Thursday, suggesting Smith is trending closer to probable than questionable. If she's cleared, Brianna Turner's minutes would likely dip.
injuries.shortComment: Smith is questionable to face the Liberty on Thursday due to an illness.

injuries.longComment: Barker will end up missing the entire 2026 season due to a leg injury. She was selected by the Aces with the No. 29 pick of the 2026 WNBA Draft, but she'll have to wait to make her professional debut until the 2027 season.
injuries.shortComment: Barker (leg) will be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season, Callie Fin of USA Today reports.

injuries.longComment: Plum suffered a left leg injury at the end of June and was projected to be sidelined for at least four weeks. While not much has been revealed regarding her current condition, she should at least be viewed as day-to-day. Plum's next opportunity to suit up will come Sunday in Portland. In the meantime, Rae Burrell is expected to remain in the starting lineup.
injuries.shortComment: Plum (leg) is listed as out for Tuesday's game versus New York.

injuries.longComment: Cechova suffered a non-contact injury during Thursday's 90-86 win over Dallas and required assistance off the floor. After undergoing an MRI, she was diagnosed with a torn ACL, ending her season. The 21-year-old rookie appeared in three games, and she will finish the 2026 campaign by averaging 8.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 0.3 steals and 0.7 blocks across 17.3 minutes. With Cechova sidelined, Anastasiia Kosu could be first in line to see more action.
injuries.shortComment: Cechova (knee) was diagnosed with a torn ACL in her right knee and will undergo surgery, Meghan L. Hall of USA Today reports. She will miss the remainder of the season.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: Johannes has missed the Liberty's last three regular-season games because of a left leg injury. If Johannes can't return Thursday, Rebecca Allen could make her fourth consecutive start. However, Allen hasn't played the best with the starters, so there's a chance she will move back to the bench.
injuries.shortComment: Johannes (ankle) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against Las Vegas.

injuries.longComment: Fiebich "avoided serious injury" and is "progressing very well," according to coach Chris DeMarco. However, the Liberty are going to take a cautious approach moving forward. A return in July seems unlikely at this point.
injuries.shortComment: Fiebich (foot) currently doesn't have a timetable to return, Jackie Powell of The IX Sports reports.

injuries.longComment: Ciezki is permitted to suit up for 12 regular-season contests while signed to a developmental contract. She has appeared in two games during the 2026 campaign, and her next opportunity to play will come Saturday against New York.
injuries.shortComment: Ciezki (coach's decision) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Golden State.

injuries.longComment: Dunn agreed to a developmental contract Sunday, so she is limited to 12 regular-season appearances. Her next chance to suit up will come Saturday against the Liberty.
injuries.shortComment: Dunn (coach's decision) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Golden State.

injuries.longComment: Nogic had her contract temporarily suspended June 20 and will now be out for the remainder of the WNBA season, as she's slated to compete overseas in Russia with an eye on leading the Serbian national team in the EuroBasket 2027 qualifiers. The guard appeared in 16 games (seven starts) for Phoenix, averaging 10.4 points, 1.6 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 20.2 minutes per contest. With Nogic out of the fold for the foreseeable future, Alexa Held stands to continue benefiting from expanded opportunities in the backcourt.
injuries.shortComment: Nogic (not injury related) intends to play professionally in Russia and won't return to Phoenix this season, Aya Abdeen of TheIXSports.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Barker was helped to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's loss to the Wings, and she's now been diagnosed with a season-ending injury. The second-year guard took on a significant role for the Fire after the club selected her in the 2026 WNBA Expansion Draft. Across 26 regular-season games (15 starts), the 24-year-old averaged 10.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per contest. Karlie Samuelson, Teja Oblak and Nyadiew Puoch are candidates for increased playing time in Barker's stead.
injuries.shortComment: The Fire announced Friday that Barker will undergo surgery to repair a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

injuries.longComment: Feagin agreed to a developmental contract with Portland on June 24 after spending time in Los Angeles. After appearing in 16 regular-season games for the Sparks in 2025, the 23-year-old played in only three regular-season contests in 2026, logging a combined 10 minutes. Feagin had yet to make her debut with the Fire, though that will now need to wait, assuming Portland keeps her on the roster moving ahead.
injuries.shortComment: Feagin (knee) was diagnosed with a torn left ACL on Thursday and will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.

injuries.longComment: Malonga was initially listed as questionable but has since been ruled out for Seattle's first contest after the All-Star break due to a back issue. Jordan Horston will get the starting nod in Malonga's stead. The 20-year-old center's next chance to suit up will come Friday in Atlanta.
injuries.shortComment: Malonga (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Fever, Percy Allen of The Seattle Times reports.

injuries.longComment: Mair is signed to a developmental contract and capped at 12 regular-season games. She last saw action during the 112-110 loss to Dallas on June 22, marking her third appearance of the 2026 campaign. Mair's next opportunity to suit up will come Friday against Atlanta.
injuries.shortComment: Mair (coach's decision) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against the Fever.

injuries.longComment: Although it wasn't specified how long Magbegor will be sidelined, it appears she will miss a significant amount of time, considering she might not be evaluated again for at least two weeks. The 26-year-old, who missed the start of the 2026 campaign because of a foot injury, has appeared in only four regular-season games. In those contests, she has averaged a career-low 3.5 points while adding 4.0 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 0.5 steals and 0.8 blocks over 13.5 minutes per contest. While Magbegor didn't see much action before her latest injury, her absence should open up more minutes for Dominique Malonga and Stefanie Dolson.
injuries.shortComment: Magbegor (face) was diagnosed with a facial fracture and will be "reevaluated in the next couple of weeks," Percy Allen of the Seattle Times reports.

injuries.longComment: Sabally is attempting to avoid sitting out a third consecutive contest Thursday with a rib injury. Laura Juskaite would likely continue to shoulder a heavy workload in the frontcourt if Sabally is unable to give it a go.
injuries.shortComment: Sabally (ribs) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Lynx.

injuries.longComment: Harrison is trying to avoid missing back-to-back contests with the issue Thursday. Temi Fagbenle would be worth streaming in most fantasy leagues if Harrison is ultimately downgraded to out, while Teonni Key could be worth a look in deeper formats in this case.
injuries.shortComment: Harrison is questionable for Thursday's game against the Lynx due to left knee soreness.

injuries.longComment: Sykes has been sidelined since June 16 due to a plantar fascia injury and has recently taken part in individual activities during practice, but it seems the veteran is still a long way from returning to game action. Her extended absence has been notable for the Tempo, as Sykes averaged 20.1 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.3 steals in 15 contests before being hampered by injury.
injuries.shortComment: Tempo head coach Sandy Brondello indicated Sunday that Sykes (foot) isn't close to returning to game action, Ian Finlayson of Sportsnet reports.

injuries.longComment: Littlepage-Buggs was activated for Washington's last three games before the All-Star break, though she didn't see the floor in any of them. She will sit out Tuesday's contest to preserve her eligibility under a developmental pact, and her next chance to play will come Friday against the Wings.
injuries.shortComment: Littlepage-Buggs (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Sun, Jenn Hatfield of The Next reports.
